rootCauseExplanation: Male, age 19, with progressive Norwood-1 pattern thinning concentrated at crown/temporal regions, and minimal active shedding. The pattern topology (terminal-to-vellus transition without diffuse shed) is the definitional signature of androgen-driven miniaturization. Pathway activation is dominated by follicular miniaturization (≥0.60) with the telogen pathway only modestly activated, which the cause registry's log-likelihood weights resolve into a dominant posterior for androgen-driven miniaturization. The case therefore leads on the androgenic cause with the standard MPHL protocol class and Norwood-grade-locked kit gating.
biologicalMechanismExplanation: DHT-driven dermal-papilla signalling shortens anagen and reduces follicle volume across successive cycles. Each cycle produces a progressively finer, shorter, and lighter hair until terminal-to-vellus transformation. Follicular architecture is preserved early and degrades with sustained exposure; partial reversibility is possible with timely intervention.

rootCauseExplanation: 26-year-old woman with PCOS diagnosis and metabolic features, oily scalp, pattern thinning at crown, Grade 2 severity, family history positive. biologicalMechanismExplanation: Perturbation of the thyroid, androgen, or estrogen axes modulates follicle cycling. Hypothyroid states prolong telogen; androgen excess (PCOS) drives miniaturization via follicular sensitivity to DHT; declining estrogen at peri/menopause withdraws an anagen-protective signal. Phenotype tracks the dominant axis.

protocolRecommendation.narrative: Endocrine optimisation upstream of hair therapy; hair-directed components run in parallel but the named lever is endocrine. Therapy axes engaged: Endocrine optimisation, DHT suppression, Scalp inflammation control, Metabolic optimisation.

expectedOutcomes: Hair response lags endocrine correction by 8–12 weeks. Full expected response window is 6–9 months from endocrine stabilisation.

rootCauseExplanation: 22-year-old female presenting with diffuse synchronized shedding lagging a clear precipitant (post-fever) by the expected 2–4 month telogen cycle. Shedding intensity (100–200 hairs/day), acute duration, and absence of pattern topology produce a dominant telogen-cycle-disruption activation. Architectural follicle integrity is preserved — this is cycle-timing pathology, fully reversible, and protocol class TE_ACUTE applies with cycle-restoration and stress-downregulation therapy needs.
biologicalMechanismExplanation: Stress-axis activation accelerates anagen-to-telogen transition. A wave of synchronized follicles enters telogen simultaneously, shedding the dormant club hairs approximately 2–4 months after the precipitant. The follicle bulb is intact; growth resumes spontaneously once the precipitant resolves.

protocolRecommendation.narrative: Cycle-restoration protocol with stress-axis downregulation and pre-emptive substrate repletion to support the rebound anagen wave. Reversibility is the dominant message; no permanent loss is expected from the current episode. Therapy axes engaged: Hair-cycle restoration, Stress-axis downregulation, Nutritional repletion.

expectedOutcomes: Active shedding subsides within 8–16 weeks. New growth visible from 12–16 weeks. Full visual recovery generally at 6–9 months, longer for chronic phenotypes.
patientNarrative: A stress event 2–4 months ago pushed many hairs into a resting phase, which now shows up as visible shedding. This is fully reversible. Most regrowth happens over the next 4–6 months as the cycle resets.
